builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Sustainable Federated Fine-Tuning with LoRA: Environmental Impact and Performance Footprint
summary: The method replaces standard federated fine-tuning configurations that use higher local step counts (100) with a constrained budget (10 steps) while applying LoRA to LLMs. It requires implementing federated averaging infrastructure and accepting that the energy-optimal configuration depends on specific hardware and model scale; the observed 6-8x energy reduction applies specifically to the tested 135M-360M parameter range on A40 and RTX 6000 Ada GPUs. Extrapolating these efficiency gains to larger foundation models or different hardware architectures may not hold, and reducing local steps could alter convergence dynamics in ways not captured by the tested accuracy metrics.
rationale: The reader can apply LoRA with reduced local steps on their 24GB GPU to potentially reduce energy costs, but must first validate that 10 local steps maintain convergence for their specific model and data distribution.
technique: Federated LoRA fine-tuning with reduced local steps

claims.statement: The method replaces standard federated fine-tuning configurations that use higher local step counts (100) with a constrained budget (10 steps) while applying LoRA to LLMs. It requires implementing federated averaging infrastructure and accepting that the energy-optimal configuration depends on specific hardware and model scale; the observed 6-8x energy reduction applies specifically to the tested 135M-360M parameter range on A40 and RTX 6000 Ada GPUs. Extrapolating these efficiency gains to larger foundation models or different hardware architectures may not hold, and reducing local steps could alter convergence dynamics in ways not captured by the tested accuracy metrics.
Configurations with fewer local steps achieved comparable accuracy with roughly 6-8-fold lower energy consumption and higher accuracy per kWh on A40 and RTX 6000 Ada GPUs.
